headline: Hi-C contact maps treated as 2D inputs for compact, task-specific and foundation-model-based architectures
label: Matrix Native Hi C Deep
summary: Three Hi-C methods this week, covering scHi-C subcompartments, TAD boundaries and map enhancement, adapt architectures to the contact-matrix representation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the treatment of Hi-C contact matrices as two-dimensional inputs for task-specific deep architectures. scSTEC annotates subcompartments from individual single-cell Hi-C matrices via direct 2D embedding and chromosome-wise consensus, without imputation or cross-cell information. AxialTAD predicts TAD boundaries with an Axial Contrast Module and reports 76-80% fewer parameters than deepTAD. HiCP2GAN uses a pretrained Vision Transformer Hi-C foundation model as discriminator in a plug-and-play GAN to enhance low-resolution contact maps. What is new is the matrix-native design: per-cell analysis without imputation, parameter compactness, and reuse of foundation-model representations in generative enhancement. These are separate tasks rather than one shared model. The remaining items concern spatial transcriptomics, histology and perturbation modeling, and are tangential to this thread.
